transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you and what brings you in today?

I guess… it’s my eating. At night, after everyone’s gone to bed, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers. But then sometimes it turns into a lot more—like half a tray of pasta from work, dessert from a client dinner, snacks from the pantry… all in one sitting. It’s embarrassing, but that’s why I’m here.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?
Not really… I don’t think of it like that. I mostly just feel bad afterward and try to ignore it.
During these times when you're eating a lot, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating?

Yes… that’s probably the worst part. Once I start, especially if it’s been a tense night with my husband, it feels like I sort of… switch off. I’ll be thinking, “Patricia, stop, that’s enough,” but I keep reaching for more anyway.
Do these episodes of eating a lot cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life, like at work or with your relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still doing my job. I’m not falling apart at work or anything. But the next morning I feel really drained, and embarrassed, and I’ve started canceling things—like yoga, or time I’d set aside to do something creative—because I just don’t want to see anyone.
How often do these episodes of eating a lot happen—like how many times a week or month?

Um… I’d say for the last few months, maybe three months, it’s been at least once most weeks. Usually at night. Some weeks it happens twice, especially if there’s been an argument or I’m coming home late from work.
